claims.head: Bodies will fly
claims.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 112.
claims.body: Boston’s hit score is 107 (10th of 32) and San Jose’s is 116 (4th). 100 is league average, after adjusting for each arena’s scorer.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 4 games this season

check.measure: hits per 60 in close games, both teams, as a score against league average (arena-adjusted)
check.rule: held if tonight's combined hit score is at or above the two teams' average; partly if above 100; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Boston keeps shots outside; San Jose lets them in
claims.body: On quality allowed, Boston sits 13th of 32, at the sheltered end of the scale. San Jose is 29th, at the exposed end.
claims.call: Boston keeps the shots it allows further from danger than San Jose does.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 4 games this season

check.rule: held if the team comes out ahead by at least half its usual margin; partly if it comes out ahead by less; otherwise didn't happen

notes.text: C. McAvoy has not played this season. M. Lohrei is in his usual spot beside J. Aspirot, up from third-pair minutes last season. That pair is getting 15:08 a game at 5-on-5, up from 12:59 with McAvoy. W. Borgen has moved into Lohrei’s old spot beside H. Lindholm.

SJS.head: San Jose starts a half-step ahead
SJS.body: The two have been about even at controlling the play lately and San Jose has home ice. Boston can still swing it if its power play gets going.

BOS.head: Boston starts a half-step behind
BOS.body: The two have been about even at controlling the play lately and San Jose has home ice. Boston can tip it if its power play gets going.
